topic.readerProblem: A marketer or founder wants to know how ChatGPT decides which web pages to cite or draw on, and which parts of that process they can influence.
topic.connection: Explains the retrieval and memory routes that determine whether ChatGPT names or cites a brand, which is exactly what AEOeye's free audit measures with live ChatGPT answers.

assessment: The page separates what OpenAI documents (when ChatGPT searches, query rewriting, partner providers, OAI-SearchBot eligibility, noindex behaviour, GPTBot independence, training sources) from what published research observed (earned-media tilt in a 2025 preprint, GEO tactics tested on a research engine and Perplexity) and from AEOeye's own inference, and labels each. It uses AEOeye's crawler access study for the OAI-SearchBot block rates and the e-commerce challenge rate, with the sample caveats. It deliberately does not claim any ranking weights, a Bing-only pipeline, that memory answers can be told apart from search answers, or that the 2025 research models equal today's ChatGPT.

sources.supports: ChatGPT may search automatically; typically rewrites a question into targeted queries and may send further queries after reviewing results; memories can shape rewrites; partners with other search providers (Microsoft and Shopify privacy statements linked); responses may include citations; results and citations can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect; ranks results using multiple factors, placement not guaranteed; eligibility = allow OAI-SearchBot and allow OpenAI's published IPs. Read in the built-in browser because the help centre returns 403 to fetchers.

OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; opted-out sites are not shown in answers but can appear as navigational links; ~24 hours for robots.txt changes; GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot are independent settings; disallowing GPTBot means content should not be used for training (confirmed in raw HTML).

Any public website can appear in ChatGPT search; don't block OAI-SearchBot; a disallowed page may still surface as link and title if the URL comes from a third-party provider; use noindex, which must be crawlable to be read; ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral URLs.
Models are developed from public internet information, third-party partner data and user/trainer-provided data; models do not store copies of training data and do not copy and paste from it.

October 2024 launch post: ChatGPT search leverages third-party search providers and content provided directly by partners; named publisher partners include Associated Press, Financial Times and Reuters.

Chen et al. (Sept 2025): AI search shows a systematic bias toward earned media over brand-owned and social content; US consumer-electronics queries, AI search 92.1% earned vs Google 32.9% brand / 15.4% social (confirmed in the PDF text; the AI model was gpt-4o-search-preview).

Aggarwal et al. (KDD 2024): Cite Sources, Quotation Addition and Statistics Addition gave 30-40% relative improvement on Position-Adjusted Word Count and 15-30% on Subjective Impression; keyword stuffing performed poorly; tested on GEO-bench with a custom engine and Perplexity.ai (confirmed in the PDF text).
Definition link for retrieval-augmented generation (page exists, HTTP 200).
